section_summary: This section traces U.S. efforts to set civil aviation policy for occupied Japan, including requests to operate airlines, proposed routes, SCAP licensing, and debate over internal service and cabotage. State, military, airline, and British correspondence shows the policy moving through the Air Coordinating Committee, SWNCC, and Far Eastern Commission. By 1948, officials were reconsidering the proposed international policy in light of security concerns and the expected length of the occupation.

subfiles.title: Request for research on Japanese civil aviation and aeronautical industry
subfiles.to: Richard Hartshorne, Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Requests OSS research to support postwar U.S. policy on Japanese aviation.
subfiles.summary: Asks for accounts of prewar Japanese aviation and the aeronautical industry, and for possible methods of enforcing U.S. policy, with material needed before July 16, 1945.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to SCAP about civilian air transport
subfiles.to: SCAP, Tokyo, for Acting Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Requests the status of airline applications and SCAP's governing policy.
subfiles.summary: Asks about applications and civilian air transport within, to, and from Japan.

subfiles.title: SCAP report on commercial airline applications
subfiles.about: Reports no applications and explains current aviation restrictions.
subfiles.summary: No commercial applications had arrived; Japanese could not operate aircraft, and military transport served occupation needs.

subfiles.title: Replacement record-copy notice
subfiles.about: Identifies a replacement record copy of the April 4 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Records that the yellow action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: SCAP report on commercial airline applications
subfiles.about: Repeats SCAP's report on applications and restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Information copy of the April 4 telegram on airline applications and the ban on Japanese aircraft operation.

subfiles.title: Procedure for preparing Japanese civil aviation policy
subfiles.about: Proposes State prepare a policy paper for Air Coordinating Committee review.
subfiles.summary: Recommends State draft the paper, obtain ACC views, and then submit it to the Directorate.

subfiles.title: U.S. policy on civil aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: Urges renewed policy work before Pan American flights begin.
subfiles.summary: Suggests asking ACC to act as the SWNCC working group to speed consideration.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about reported Japanese airline plan
subfiles.about: Seeks verification of a press report about a U.S.-managed Japanese airline network.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether MacArthur approved a reorganization plan reportedly attracting U.S. investors.

subfiles.title: U.S. policy on civil aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats the proposal for ACC to serve as a SWNCC working group.
subfiles.summary: Copy of Whitman's May 15 memorandum.

subfiles.title: Denial of reported airline reorganization plan
subfiles.about: Denies that headquarters is considering the reported airline plan.
subfiles.summary: Says commercial airlines may have ideas, but nothing concrete has materialized.

subfiles.title: Asia Airways inquiry forwarded by counsel
subfiles.about: Requests guidance for Asia Airways' application to operate within Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks which authority should receive the application and what policy may govern approval.

subfiles.title: Asia Airways request for application guidance
subfiles.about: Describes the company's application history and asks where to submit supporting papers.
subfiles.summary: Recounts the December 1945 application, incorporation, SCAP acknowledgments, and financing; asks for procedural guidance and recognition of the original filing date.

subfiles.title: SCAP acknowledgment to Asia Airways
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the airline's correspondence and forwards it to the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Recommends directing future inquiries to the War Department.

subfiles.title: Notice of Asia Airways incorporation
subfiles.about: Updates SCAP on the applicant's new corporate name.
subfiles.summary: Says Far East Air Transport Company incorporated in Delaware as Asia Airways and seeks a response to its application.

subfiles.title: Initial Far East Air Transport Company application
subfiles.from: Ernest J. Silver, Far East Air Transport Company
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests consideration of commercial airline operations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Offers a prospectus and asks SCAP to retain the application if permission is premature.

subfiles.title: Reply to Oscar Cox about Asia Airways
subfiles.about: Explains that procedures and selection criteria remain unsettled.
subfiles.summary: Says U.S. agencies are developing policy, which will require Far Eastern Commission consideration.

subfiles.title: Routing note for Cox correspondence
subfiles.about: Directs Cox's letter to the office handling earlier correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Requests referral to the responsible State Department division.

subfiles.title: Cox acknowledgment of State's reply
subfiles.about: Thanks State for its response concerning Asia Airways.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges State's promise to notify him when policy decisions become public.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about post-treaty Japanese airlines
subfiles.to: Chief, Aviation Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese nationals may operate domestic airlines after a peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Seeks any emerging policy beyond current SCAP prohibitions.

subfiles.title: Reply to Silver on post-treaty operations
subfiles.about: States that post-treaty aviation rights cannot yet be determined.
subfiles.summary: Explains that peace-treaty terms and the views of other governments remain unresolved.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on SCAP airline licenses
subfiles.about: Recommends immediate licenses for Northwest and Pan American subject to a policy directive.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes survey flights and SCAP's urgent requests. Recommends allowing licenses for planning while delaying scheduled operations until SCAP receives an interim or final directive.

subfiles.title: Revised draft reply on SCAP licenses
subfiles.about: Proposes conditional issuance of licenses to Northwest and Pan American.
subfiles.summary: Draft cable permits licenses immediately but bars scheduled operations until an interim directive arrives.

subfiles.title: Lister's transmittal of draft license reply
subfiles.about: Seeks approval and prompt dispatch of a draft response to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Calls the attached draft a reasonable compromise between JK and TRC positions.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft reply on SCAP licenses
subfiles.about: Proposes issuing licenses before scheduled airline service begins.
subfiles.summary: Would let the carriers plan operations while withholding scheduled service until SCAP receives an interim directive.

subfiles.title: Interim War Department response to SCAP
subfiles.about: Acknowledges urgency of SCAP's airline licensing inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Promises a prompt substantive reply and says Northwest is being kept informed.

subfiles.title: Northwest Airlines proposed Pacific routes
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed scheduled routes beginning around May 1, 1947.
subfiles.summary: Lists planned service linking the United States, Japan, Korea, China, and the Philippines.

subfiles.title: SCAP reminder about urgent license decision
subfiles.about: Requests a prompt answer because Northwest wishes to begin operations in May.
subfiles.summary: Refers to SCAP's March 10 licensing inquiry.

subfiles.title: SCAP request to issue airline licenses
subfiles.about: Asks whether immediate licenses would jeopardize the U.S. policy position.
subfiles.summary: SCAP is ready to license Northwest and Pan American for scheduled service.

subfiles.title: Proposal to defer airline licenses
subfiles.about: Recommends withholding licenses pending policy approval.
subfiles.summary: Draft cable tells SCAP to await a policy or interim directive.

subfiles.title: Briefing on draft Japanese aviation policy
subfiles.about: Summarizes the proposed restrictions and recommends endorsing the policy.
subfiles.summary: Reviews limits on Japanese participation, internal service, international routes, and occupation transport.

subfiles.title: Draft response to Norton
subfiles.about: Expresses preliminary satisfaction with the proposed aviation policy.
subfiles.summary: Marked as unsigned and unsent; Lister advised that Hilldring had no objection.

subfiles.title: Norton request for preliminary views
subfiles.about: Requests comments before ACC Economic Division consideration.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Japanese draft policy, the approved German policy, and a memorandum on airline licenses.

subfiles.title: ACC policy on civil aviation in Germany
subfiles.about: Sets U.S. policy for civil aviation during Germany's occupation.
subfiles.summary: The paper weighs security against economic recovery, limits German participation and internal airlines, and allows controlled international service. It assigns aviation facilities and technical rules to occupation authorities, with fees and PICAO standards.

subfiles.title: Norton memorandum and proposed cable on airline licenses
subfiles.about: Argues that SCAP can license Northwest and Pan American before policy approval.
subfiles.summary: Norton describes the carriers' planning needs and the proposed U.S. aviation policy. The draft cable outlines permitted international routes, limits on internal service, control of facilities, Japanese employment restrictions, and fees, while saying licenses need not jeopardize the U.S. position.

subfiles.title: Draft U.S. policy on civil aviation in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes occupation-period rules for Japanese civil aviation.
subfiles.summary: The draft seeks to prevent renewed military aviation while allowing limited air services for occupation and economic recovery. It bars Japanese flight operations and separate domestic airlines, gives SCAP control over international services and facilities, and permits restricted employment of Japanese ground personnel. It recommends ACC, military, SWNCC, and Far Eastern Commission consideration.

subfiles.title: SCAP orders abolishing Japanese civil aviation
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Orders abolition of Japanese civil aviation bodies and activities.
subfiles.summary: Requires dissolution and registration of aviation personnel and bans Japanese aircraft ownership, operations, and aeronautical instruction or research.

subfiles.title: Questions from SCAP about Pacific air routes
subfiles.about: Relays SCAP questions about licensed airlines and a proposed Shanghai–Wake route.
subfiles.summary: SCAP requests carrier lists and questions whether China National Aviation Corporation may use Northwest's route.

subfiles.title: Submission of civil aviation paper to SWNCC
subfiles.about: Requests circulation of State's civil aviation policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Submits State Department views for committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Japanese aircraft pictures
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Lyon
subfiles.about: Responds to René Fautre's request for pictures of Japanese aircraft.
subfiles.summary: Asks the consul to forward four pages from Aircraft Spotter.

subfiles.title: Fragmentary Shanghai telegram on internal air service
subfiles.about: Reports discussions concerning internal aviation policy and discriminatory treatment.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is fragmentary; the telegram concerns Far Eastern Commission debate over internal service and cabotage.

subfiles.title: Instructions to Shanghai on cabotage amendment
subfiles.about: Explains British and Chinese positions on internal service in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State seeks interagency views while continuing to favor SCAP authority to grant limited cabotage.

subfiles.title: London despatch on British internal air service policy
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy London
subfiles.about: Forwards a conversation memorandum about the British position.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Embassy presented State's views to the Foreign Office before receiving contrary instructions.

subfiles.title: Conversation with British Foreign Office officials
subfiles.about: Records British views on cabotage and a separate internal airline.
subfiles.summary: MacDermot and Cheke say Britain opposed cabotage because SCAP military service appeared sufficient. They distinguish a post-treaty Japanese airline proposal from occupation policy and suggest a joint international company is now impractical.

subfiles.title: London despatch forwarding British policy letter
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy London
subfiles.about: Forwards a Foreign Office statement on Japanese civil aviation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses MacDermot's November 25 letter explaining British policy.

subfiles.title: Foreign Office position on Japanese cabotage
subfiles.about: Explains British support for deferring internal civil service pending FEC review.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office doubts current demand for domestic flights and fears cabotage could prejudge post-occupation aviation. It favors a Chinese proposal requiring SCAP to seek an FEC policy decision before internal civil service begins.

subfiles.title: Pan American application for Japanese domestic points
subfiles.about: Reports Pan American's application for additional routes within Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lists proposed Japanese stops and says State is asking the Civil Aeronautics Board to defer action until the Far Eastern Commission decides the cabotage question.

subfiles.title: CAB response on Pan American application
subfiles.about: Agrees to defer procedural action on Pan American's application.
subfiles.summary: No action will be taken until the policy situation is clarified.

subfiles.title: U.S.–British discussion of FEC aviation paper
subfiles.about: Records an informal effort to find a U.S.–British compromise on internal service.
subfiles.summary: Thayer argues that the FEC draft unduly restricts SCAP during a longer occupation. Participants discuss limiting cabotage by definition or time, while British officials say they remain instructed to support the Chinese amendment. They agree the British side will seek further views from London.

subfiles.title: Army objections to FEC civil aviation draft
subfiles.about: Challenges changes to the U.S. aviation proposal under FEC consideration.
subfiles.summary: Draper argues the revised draft weakens SCAP's discretion, treats occupying and other powers alike, and risks a Soviet veto over internal aviation. He links the issue to changing U.S. security priorities and urges SANACC and Joint Chiefs review before further FEC action.

subfiles.title: State reply on reconsidering FEC civil aviation policy
subfiles.about: Describes State's revised position and requests prompt interagency agreement.
subfiles.summary: Wisner says the U.S. representative has deferred FEC action while policy is reviewed. State has circulated a proposed position to Army and Air Force officials; he favors SCAP comment and hopes for agreement before the July 1 Commission meeting.
